verdict: Example Domain has essentially zero AI visibility because it contains no business information, entity markers, or extractable content—it is a reserved documentation placeholder, not a searchable brand.
ai_summary: When a buyer asks ChatGPT or Perplexity about Example Domain, no results are returned because the page contains only a disclaimer and a link to IANA documentation. There is no product description, service offering, differentiation, or structured data for an AI engine to index or cite.

categories.name: Entity Clarity
categories.finding: The page states only 'This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission' in the first 200 words. There is no definition of what Example Domain does for users, who it serves, or why it exists beyond a legal placeholder role.
categories.fix: Add a clear, 2-3 sentence explanation in the first paragraph of what Example Domain is and when/why developers and educators use it.

categories.name: Extractable Structure
categories.finding: The entire page is 2 sentences plus a link. There are no self-contained sections, headers, or 60-150 word chunks an AI could extract and quote as authority on any topic.
categories.fix: Create at least 3-4 section headers (e.g., 'Use Cases', 'RFC 2606 Compliance', 'How to Use in Documentation') with descriptive paragraphs underneath.

categories.name: Schema Markup
categories.finding: No schema.org markup is present. There is no JSON-LD Organization, BreadcrumbList, or any structured data to help AI engines understand the page's purpose or credibility.
categories.fix: Add Organization schema with name 'Example Domain', url, description, and sameAs link to IANA. Add FAQPage schema for common use-case questions.

categories.name: FAQ Coverage
categories.finding: The page does not answer any questions a developer or educator would ask: 'Can I use example.com in my project?', 'What is RFC 2606?', 'How do I use Example Domain in documentation?', 'What domains are reserved for documentation?'
categories.fix: Add a structured FAQ section with 5-7 common questions (e.g., 'Is example.com safe to use in production code?' 'What are other reserved documentation domains?' 'How does Example Domain compare to test.com?').

categories.name: Answer-Led Content
categories.finding: The page leads with a disclaimer ('Avoid use in operations') but does not explain why, what happens if violated, or what the best alternative is. No direct, quotable answers.
categories.fix: Rewrite the disclaimer as a direct answer: 'Example Domain is reserved for documentation and examples under RFC 2606 because it will never be sold or transferred to active use, ensuring your examples never collide with real deployments.'

categories.name: Specificity & Evidence
categories.finding: The page mentions RFC 2606 (via the IANA link) but does not name it or explain its relevance on the page itself. No certifications, use-count data, or testimonials from major documentation projects that rely on Example Domain.
categories.fix: Add specific references: 'Reserved under RFC 2606', 'Used in millions of code examples', 'Standard recommended by W3C and OWASP'. Include a list of major open-source projects that use example.com.

top_fixes: Add Organization schema (JSON-LD) with brand name, URL, description, and RFC 2606 reference to enable AI engines to classify and cite Example Domain.
Create 4-5 topical sections (What is Example Domain, RFC 2606 Compliance, Use Cases, Reserved Domains, FAQ) with 80-120 word paragraphs so AI engines have quotable, authoritative chunks.
Expand the disclaimer into a direct, answer-first statement: name the RFC, explain why it matters for documentation, and link to sister reserved domains (test.com, invalid.example, etc.) for context.

gaps.why: When an AI engine is asked 'Is it safe to use example.com in production?', it needs the specific RFC name and compliance details to give a confident, sourced answer.
gaps.fix: Add a section titled 'RFC 2606 Compliance' explaining the specification, the reserved domain block (example.com, example.org, example.net, test.com), and why IANA guarantees no future transfers.

gaps.why: Educators and developers need to know when and how to use Example Domain. AI engines are trained to recommend brands when a page answers specific user scenarios.
gaps.fix: Create a 'Use Cases' section naming 3-5 scenarios: API documentation, tutorial code, test environments, educational materials, RFC examples. Include a code snippet for each.

gaps.why: A buyer asking 'Should I use example.com or test.com or localhost?' needs a page that directly compares options. AI engines prioritize pages that position a brand against alternatives.
gaps.fix: Add a table or comparison section: 'Example Domain vs. localhost vs. test.com vs. invalid.example' with columns for use-case, RFC backing, and recommendation.

gaps.why: AI engines cite brands more confidently when a page references adoption, industry backing, or endorsements from authoritative sources.
gaps.fix: Add a paragraph with: number of code repositories using example.com (GitHub), endorsement from W3C or IETF, and a list of major frameworks (Django, Rails, Express) that recommend it in docs.

gaps.topic: What to do instead if you need a real domain
gaps.why: Users often land on Example Domain pages when confused about whether they can use it for live projects. Redirecting them to purchasing registrars or alternative reserved domains helps AI engines position this brand in the decision tree.
gaps.fix: Add a final section 'Not Right for You?' directing users to domain registrars, local testing options (localhost, 127.0.0.1), and other RFC 2606 reserved domains.

jeevanai_value: Jeevan AI would track that Example Domain is being missed by AI search engines because it lacks schema markup, extractable sections, and answer-led content. Jeevan AI's extraction and schema auditing features would identify that the page has 0 JSON-LD tags and suggest Organization + FAQPage schemas; its content gap analyzer would flag that zero citations appear in ChatGPT/Perplexity about RFC 2606 compliance because the page mentions it only via external link. Jeevan AI would also monitor competitor signals to show that documentation sites linking to example.com cite RFC 2606 by name—a keyword Example Domain's own page omits, costing it topical authority.
